chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Az-Zubayr remained a man from us, the Ahl al-Bayt, until his wretched son 'Abdullah came forth.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House, referring to the Prophet's family and close kin.
key_terms.الزُّبَيْرُ: Az-Zubayr, a prominent companion and cousin of the Prophet.
key_terms.الْمَشْؤُومُ: The wretched or ill-fated, indicating a negative fate or betrayal.

ai.seo_question: Why did Az-Zubayr cease to be considered part of the Ahl al-Bayt according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) declares that Az-Zubayr remained a true member of the Ahl al-Bayt as long as his son, Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, did not rise to prominence, implying that the son's eventual betrayal severed the familial bond of spiritual and political alignment. This statement highlights the Shia perspective that kinship to the Prophet is not merely genealogical but contingent upon adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt's cause, a status lost when Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr diverged from their path.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 453. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
az-Zubayr remained a man from our house till his wretched son ‘Abdullāh came forth. [1]
